sources.title: An interview with Dr. Stuart Russell, author of "Human Compatible: Artificial Intelligence and the Problem of Control"
sources.quote_checked: I don't want the machine to have any values, other than what it is that humans want. | It has to come with a proof that it doesn't get out of control. | I've been thinking about this problem – what if we succeed with AI? – on and off since the early 90s.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Aligned with Human Values? Q&A with Stuart Russell
sources.quote_checked: I don't see any real way around the fact that there's going to be, in some sense, a values industry. | What if we do succeed?

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Will Do What We Ask. That's a Problem.
sources.quote_checked: If we cannot switch a machine off because it won't let us, we're really in trouble. | uncertainty about the objective is essential for ensuring that we can switch the machine off | the core of the problem of control for intelligent systems

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence and the King Midas Problem
sources.quote_checked: It's the old King Midas problem. | We don't have to know what we want. That's the whole point. | what we ask for is evidence for what we really want

sources.title: Toward Human-Centric A.I.
sources.quote_checked: provably safe A.I. | Most of the ways you can put a purpose into a machine are going to be wrong.

sources.title: How to keep AI from killing us all
sources.quote_checked: We're basically saying that you can't turn on artificial general intelligence until you've shown that it's safe. | Intelligence gives you power over the world | the kinds of capabilities that would be a big flashing red light for the human race

sources.title: Musk, Wozniak and 1,100+ Others 'Pause Giant AI Experiments'
sources.quote_checked: Stuart Russell, Berkeley professor of Computer Science, director of the Center for Intelligent Systems
